_about: Junius–Tremellius chapter divisions, read off the page images of testamentiveteri00trem
(Hanau 1603). This is the table that answers 'what did Milton's Bible call this verse?',
where tools/versification.json answers 'could this verse exist?'. M4-RUNBOOK §11–13.
MODEL. One entry says: J–T's chapter <book> <chapter> begins at KJV <begins_at>, and its
first verse carries the number <first_verse>. Everything else follows by walking forward
through the KJV verse counts in versification.json, crossing chapter boundaries as needed.
That one shape covers all four mechanisms actually observed:
· a chapter that starts early or late   (Num 23, Prov 12, Eccl 4, Isa 44, Isa 57, …)
· a chapter whose verse count does NOT restart   (Ezek 3, first_verse 11)
· a psalm whose superscription is numbered   (Ps 54 first_verse 3, Ps 55 first_verse 2)
· a verse printed above the received rubric   (1 Sam 16, begins at KJV 15:35)
⚠ status 'read' means a page image was read and the evidence quoted. 'inferred' means the
offset is constant and content-checked across the chapter but the boundary verse itself was
not put in view. Nothing here is a guess; a guess does not go in this file.
_psalms_rule: The Psalms are a class, not a list. J–T (following the Hebrew) NUMBERS THE SUPERSCRIPTION:
a one-line title takes verse 1, a two-line title takes verses 1–2, and a psalm with no title
has no offset at all. Confirmed on leaf 458, where Ps LIIII (two-line, 'Quum venientes
Ziphæi…') and Ps LV (one-line) sit on one opening with +2 and +1 respectively.
So a Psalm divergence of exactly +1 or +2 has a KNOWN MECHANISM even where that psalm's own
leaf has not been read — which is what the 'versification-predicted' class records.

divisions.evidence: CAPUT XXIII opens 'Dixit verò Bilham Balako, ecce veni ad te' = KJV 22:38
J–T 35 = KJV 11:33 'Percussit enim eorum à Harohere', 36 = 11:34, 41 = 11:39
verse 1 'Posteà non perrexit Schemuel' (= KJV 15:35) is printed ABOVE the CAPUT XVI rubric; KJV 16:1 is numbered 2
superscription numbered as TWO verses: 1 'Magistro symphoniæ à fidium', 2 'Quum venientes Ziphæi dixissent Schauli'
one-line superscription numbered as verse 1; J–T 18 = KJV 55:17 'Vespere & mane atq; meridie meditabor'
J–T 18 = KJV 12:19 'Labium verax stabilitur in æternum'; the chapter closes at 27 where the KJV closes at 28
J–T's chapter I closes at 17 = KJV 1:17, so CAPUT II takes KJV 1:18
CAPUT IIII opens at 'Stolidus complicat manus suas' = KJV 4:5; J–T ch. III ran on as verses 23–26
J–T 9:3 = KJV 9:1 'Nam totum hoc condidi in animo meo'; the scholion argues it: 'duos hosce versus omnino ad sequentia pertinere res ipsa loquitur'
J–T 13, 14 = KJV 10:16, 17 'Hei tibi regio, cujus rex puer est'; six consecutive verses check
constant +1 across the chapter: J–T 5 = KJV 3:4, 8 = 3:7, 11 = 3:10, 13 = 3:12, 15 = 3:14, 19 = 3:18; J–T's own scholion divides men from women at v. 17 where the KJV has 3:16
J–T ch. XLIII runs on to 20 = KJV 44:5 'de nomine Jisraëlis cognominabit'; CAPUT XLIV opens at KJV 44:6
CAPUT LVII opens 'Omnes bestiæ agrestes, venite ad comedendum' = KJV 56:9; its 2 is 'Speculatores istius cæci' = KJV 56:10
ch. II ends at 10 as the KJV's does; CAPUT III then opens AT VERSE 11 'Edixit igitur mihi, fili hominis' = KJV 3:1, running unbroken to 25 = KJV 3:15
